title: Warm/fast reboot non-functional on Nexthop NH-4010/NH-4210: ASIC power-cycled on syncd stop, SAI warm-boot state file not configured
author: wren-nexthop
body:
**Description**

Warm reboot and fast reboot do not work on the Nexthop NH-4010 and NH-4210 platforms, for two reasons:

1. The hwsku `sai.profile` files for NH-4010 (x86_64-nexthop_4010-r1) and NH-4210 (x86_64-nexthop_4210-r0021) are missing the Broadcom SAI warm-boot state file keys (`SAI_KEY_WARM_BOOT_WRITE_FILE` / `SAI_KEY_WARM_BOOT_READ_FILE`), so SAI never writes or restores `/var/warmboot/sai-warmboot.bin` across the kexec.
2. The per-platform `syncd.service.d` overrides (`nh-4010/.../ge-override.conf`, `nh-4210/.../sea-eagle-override.conf`) run `ExecStopPost=/usr/local/bin/asic_init.sh` unconditionally. This power-cycles the ASIC on every syncd stop — including the syncd stop that happens during warm/fast reboot orchestration — destroying the preserved dataplane state.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Boot an NH-4010 or NH-4210 with a current image built from this repo (also reproduces on the msft-202512 branch).
2. Run `fast-reboot` (or `warm-reboot`).

**Observed behavior**

The ASIC is power-cycled during shutdown, so the dataplane is not preserved and the reboot degrades to a cold-boot-like path. (An additional, separate issue on 202512-based images — a hard reset ~55s after the kexec boot — is what makes sonic-mgmt `test_fast_reboot` fail its reboot-cause check there; that is tracked separately. This issue covers the missing plumbing itself.)

**Expected behavior**

Warm/fast reboot keeps the ASIC and dataplane intact across kexec, and `show reboot-cause` reports the corresponding cause afterwards.

linkedPullRequests.title: [Nexthop] Enable warm/fast reboot plumbing on NH-4010 and NH-4210
linkedPullRequests.author: wren-nexthop
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

Resolves #28655

Warm and fast reboot are non-functional on the Nexthop NH-4010 and NH-4210 platforms:

1. The hwsku `sai.profile` files are missing the Broadcom SAI warm-boot state file keys, so SAI never writes/restores `/var/warmboot/sai-warmboot.bin` across the kexec.
2. The per-platform `syncd.service.d` overrides run `ExecStopPost=/usr/local/bin/asic_init.sh` unconditionally, power-cycling the ASIC on every syncd stop — including during warm/fast reboot orchestration, which destroys the preserved dataplane.
3. On the post-kexec boot, `pre_pddf_init.sh` runs `asic_init.sh` unconditionally, fully resetting the ASIC after a warm reboot and destroying the dataplane state the shutdown side preserved. In addition, ASIC interrupts left enabled by the pre-kexec kernel can fire when the driver reloads — before userspace remaps the BARs — and panic the kernel.

Note: this PR fixes the missing plumbing itself (SAI state preservation, no ASIC power-cycle mid-orchestration, warm-aware boot-time init). The `test_fast_reboot` reboot-cause failure seen in CI on 202512-based images turned out to have an additional cause — a hard reset ~55s after the kexec boot, under separate investigation — so this PR alone is not expected to flip that test; it is a prerequisite for correct warm/fast reboot behavior.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**: N/A

#### How I did it

- Add `SAI_KEY_WARM_BOOT_WRITE_FILE` / `SAI_KEY_WARM_BOOT_READ_FILE` (`/var/warmboot/sai-warmboot.bin`) to the NH-4010 (x86_64-nexthop_4010-r1) and NH-4210 (x86_64-nexthop_4210-r0021) sai.profiles.
- Add `common/utils/syncd_post_stop.py` and point the `ge-override.conf` / `sea-eagle-override.conf` `ExecStopPost` at it. The script checks STATE_DB `WARM_RESTART_ENABLE_TABLE|system` / `FAST_RESTART_ENABLE_TABLE|system` (and `/host/warmboot/dump.rdb`) and skips the ASIC power-cycle while warm/fast reboot is in progress; on any other syncd stop it execs `asic_init.sh` exactly as before. Scripts in `common/utils/` are installed to `/usr/local/bin` by the existing debian rules.
- Add `common/utils/asic_init_wrapper.py`, invoked from `pre_pddf_init.sh` in place of `asic_init.sh`. On `SONIC_BOOT_TYPE=warm` it skips the ASIC reset and disables the ASIC's INTx/MSI/MSI-X at the PCI config-space level so a stale interrupt cannot fire while the driver reloads; on cold boot or fast-reboot post-kexec (`SONIC_BOOT_TYPE=fast-reboot`) it execs `asic_init.sh` exactly as before, and any wrapper failure falls back to the full ASIC init. The supporting setpci/interrupt-disable helpers live in `nexthop/pcie_lib.py`, with unit tests for both the library and the wrapper.

Cold boot and syncd-crash recovery behavior is unchanged.

#### How to verify it

Validated internally on NH-4210 (O256): with these changes `fast-reboot` completes successfully and sonic-mgmt `platform_tests/test_reboot.py::test_fast_reboot` passes, including the `show reboot-cause` check. Without them the ASIC is power-cycled during shutdown and the test fails as described above. NH-4010 has been running this configuration internally with warm/fast reboot tests enabled in nightly CI.

Additionally, the CI image built from this PR (Azure build 1177884, `master-28656.1177884`) was installed on NH-4010 hardware via ONIE and the plumbing verified in place: the warm-boot keys land in the sai.profiles, `syncd_post_stop.py` is installed and wired as the syncd `ExecStopPost`, and on a plain (non-warm) syncd stop it logs `syncd stop without warm/fast reboot: power-cycling ASIC to reinitialize` and runs the full ASIC init exactly as before. The `asic_init_wrapper.py` paths were exercised on the same hardware: ASIC BDF discovery from the platform `pcie-variables.yaml`, the warm-path INTx/MSI/MSI-X disable (verified via the PCI Command register), and the cold-path fallthrough to `asic_init.sh`. `test/unit` for `sonic-platform-modules-nexthop` passes (369 tests).

#### Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)

- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [x] 202512
- [ ] 202605
- [ ] 202608

Reason: Nexthop NH-4010/NH-4210 ship on 202512-based images, which currently lack this plumbing entirely (verified: no warm-boot keys in the sai.profiles, unconditional asic_init.sh ExecStopPost). The change only touches Nexthop vendor directories (`device/nexthop`, `platform/broadcom/sonic-platform-modules-nexthop`) — no common code, no other platforms affected.

Tracking issue/work item for backport/cherry-pick request (GitHub issue or Microsoft ADO): #28655
Failure type: product bug (warm/fast reboot non-functional on Nexthop platforms)

#### Tested branch

- [x] master
- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [x] 202512
- [ ] 202605
- [ ] 202608
- [ ] N/A

#### Test result

- master: the CI image built from this PR was installed on NH-4010 hardware via ONIE and the plumbing verified in place (see "How to verify it"). Also validated on NH-4210 (O256) hardware running an internal image built from master with these changes — `fast-reboot` completes successfully, and sonic-mgmt `platform_tests/test_reboot.py::test_fast_reboot` passes including the `show reboot-cause` check. NH-4010 runs this configuration in internal nightly CI with warm/fast reboot tests enabled.
- 202512: applied these exact files on NH-4210 (P128) hardware running an image built from the 202512 branch — configuration applies cleanly, syncd picks up the warm-boot keys, cold boot and BGP/interface health unaffected. End-to-end `test_fast_reboot` on this branch is currently blocked by a separate platform issue (an unexpected reset ~55s after the kexec boot, pending the watchdog upstreaming); A/B runs confirmed this PR neither causes nor masks that issue.

#### Description for the changelog

[Nexthop] Enable warm/fast reboot on NH-4010 and NH-4210: add SAI warm-boot state file keys, skip the syncd-stop ASIC power-cycle during warm/fast reboot orchestration, and make boot-time ASIC init warm-aware (skip re-init and quiesce stale PCI interrupts on the post-kexec boot).

N/A — no YANG/config_db changes.
